title: IB Social and Cultural Anthropology IA Timeline
summary: Plan your IB Social and Cultural Anthropology IA from September to November with realistic SL and HL milestones before the winter break rush.
body_markdown:
If you want your Social and Cultural Anthropology IA finished before winter break, **HL students should begin in the first week of September** and complete fieldwork by October 31. November should be reserved for analysis, writing, feedback, and final checks.


For **SL students** , the second fieldwork stage occurs **4-6 months after the initial observation** . An SL student can finish by November only if the initial observation was completed during the previous spring or early summer. Always confirm the applicable sequence and internal deadlines with your teacher.


### Check your level and school requirements


The[official IB Social and Cultural Anthropology subject brief](https://ibo.org/contentassets/5895a05412144fe890312bad52b17044/social-and-cultural-anthropology-sl-hl-2017-en.pdf) identifies different internal assessment tasks for SL and HL. Their processes and schedules are not interchangeable.


Requirement SL HL


Task Limited fieldwork and critical reflection Fieldwork investigation, proposal, report, and reflection


Recommended course time **30 hours** **60 hours**


Assessment weighting **20%** **25%**


Overall word limit **2,000 words** **2,400 words**


Timing issue Second fieldwork stage follows the observation by 4-6 months No equivalent compulsory interval


The SL allowance includes a **450-word observation report** , **300-word methodological and conceptual justification** , **400-word second fieldwork report** , and **850-word critical reflection** . HL assessed writing includes an **800-word critical reflection** and a **1,600-word research report and reflection** .


These are IB requirements. Your teacher may set earlier deadlines for approval, fieldwork, draft feedback, or authentication, so build your schedule around the school calendar rather than the final IB submission date.


### Can you finish between September and November?


### HL students


Yes, provided you begin early and work consistently. The recommended 60 hours across approximately 12 weeks equals around **5 hours per week** , including class time, reading, meetings, fieldwork, organization, and writing.


Choose an accessible field site and settle a focused question by mid-September. Projects requiring difficult travel, several external approvals, or access to vulnerable participants are unlikely to fit this schedule safely.


### SL students


If the initial observation was completed in May or June, the required interval may have elapsed by autumn. You can then complete the methodological extension, second fieldwork, and final reflection from September to November.


If the observation takes place in September, the later stage would normally begin between January and March. Your pre-winter goal should be to complete the observation report correctly and prepare for the remaining stages, not bypass the required interval.


### September-to-November HL timeline


This schedule assumes a final school deadline near the end of November. Move each stage earlier if your teacher requires an earlier draft.


Week Main task Deliverable


**September 1-7** Read the task, criteria, ethics guidance, and school calendar Deadline plan and possible settings


**September 8-14** Narrow the inquiry, site, concept, and question One feasible question and a backup


**September 15-21** Select at least two methods and begin relevant reading Method, access, and source plan


**September 22-30** Deliver the proposal and consider panel feedback Revised proposal and change record


**October 1-7** Complete the critical reflection and ethical preparations Reflection draft and consent materials


**October 8-21** Conduct the main fieldwork Organized field notes and approved records


**October 22-31** Close data collection and identify themes Anonymized evidence and 3-5 findings


**November 1-9** Draft context, concepts, methods, and evidence Approximately half of the report


**November 10-16** Write analysis, conclusions, and reflection Complete first draft


**November 17-23** Revise using criteria and permitted feedback Focused second draft


**November 24-30** Check citations, anonymity, word limits, and formatting Final authenticated version


Treat **October 31** as the fieldwork cutoff. Continuing deep into November usually weakens analysis because you are still collecting information while trying to interpret it.


### September-to-November SL timeline


If the initial observation was completed before summer, use September to design the extension, October for the second fieldwork, and November for analysis and reflection.


Period Priority


**September 1-15** Revisit the retained observation report and choose an explicit concept


**September 16-30** Write the method and concept justification and obtain approval


**October 1-15** Conduct the second fieldwork using the approved method


**October 16-31** Select and analyze evidence connected to the concept


**November 1-15** Draft the second fieldwork report and critical reflection


**November 16-30** Compare methods, discuss positionality, and complete final checks


If the initial observation begins in September, complete the one-hour observation and descriptive **450-word report** according to your teacher's instructions. The report is retained and should not later be rewritten using concepts learned after the observation.


Use the remaining autumn weeks to study methods, ethics, concepts, and researcher positionality. Arrange the January-to-March continuation with your teacher. In this situation, being finished before winter break means being fully on schedule, not completing the entire IA.


### Build a feasible and ethical investigation


A workable HL question examines a specific social or cultural process in an accessible setting. For example, you might investigate how status is negotiated during meetings of a school club through observation and semi-structured interviews.


Test the question against five conditions:


- **Access:** Can you enter the setting repeatedly during October?
- **Scope:** Can limited fieldwork address the question?
- **Anthropological focus:** Does it connect social practice to a concept or theory?
- **Evidence:** Will the methods produce interpretable information?
- **Ethics:** Can you maintain consent, confidentiality, and protection from harm?


Consent must be secured before participation, and collected information must be stored securely. Keep a dated research log recording access, consent, fieldwork sessions, methodological changes, positionality, and limitations. These details provide evidence for meaningful reflection later.


The IB's[guidance on artificial intelligence in assessment](https://www.ibo.org/programmes/artificial-intelligence-ai-in-learning-teaching-and-assessment/) explains that AI-generated work is not regarded as the student's own and must be acknowledged when included. Jojo AI may help you interpret criteria or test whether a plan is manageable, but it should not produce your fieldwork analysis or submission-ready reflection.


### Common scheduling mistakes


- **Waiting for the perfect question:** Choose a narrow, accessible question by mid-September.
- **Starting before approval:** Editing cannot repair fieldwork conducted without appropriate consent.
- **Confusing data with analysis:** Organize evidence into patterns, contrasts, exceptions, and relevant themes.
- **Leaving reflection until November:** Record positionality and methodological decisions after each session.
- **Extending fieldwork unnecessarily:** Protect November as a writing and revision month.
- **Ignoring the SL sequence:** Never compress the compulsory 4-6 month interval to meet a personal target.


### Keep the weekly workload manageable


During September and October, schedule two longer sessions for planning or fieldwork and one shorter session for organization. Digitize notes, anonymize participant details, and record a methodological reflection within 24 hours of every visit.


The[RevisionDojo Study Planner](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/study-planner) can place these tasks alongside other deadlines. You can also examine[Social and Cultural Anthropology coursework exemplars](https://www.revisiondojo.com/coursework-exemplars/subject/ib-social-and-cultural-anthropology) for principles of organization and analytical depth, without copying their questions or wording.


### Conclusion


An effective IB Social and Cultural Anthropology IA timeline starts in early September. HL students should finish planning during September, close fieldwork by October 31, and protect November for interpretation, reflection, and revision.


SL students must respect the required interval after their initial observation.
